summary: Morpheus leads Neo into a cramped room full of high-tech equipment where Trinity, Apoc, Switch and Cypher are working. Trinity fixes white electrode disks to Neo as he sits in a chair near a cracked oval mirror. Morpheus explains the pill Neo took is a trace program that disrupts his input/output carrier signal so they can pinpoint his location. As the crew works to bring them on-line, Neo watches the cracked mirror heal and turn liquid; when he touches it his fingers disappear into the rippling surface and stretch like taffy. The mirror gel crawls up his arms, neck and face while Trinity's monitors register fibrillation and cardiac arrest. Just as the crew locks his target, Morpheus orders Tank to send the signal; a high-pitched electric scream erupts in Neo's headphones, his body arches in agony, and everything is swallowed by darkness.

what_changes.before: A curious, slightly awed visitor being wired up, whispering to Trinity, 'You did all this?'
what_changes.after: In physical extremis as the mirror-liquid invades his body and his vitals fail: 'It's cold.' ... 'Uh-oh...' ... his body arches in agony.
what_changes.evidence: The mirror creeps up his neck as Neo begins to panic, tipping his head as though he were sinking into the mirror, trying to keep his mouth up.

what_changes.before: Skeptical and confused about what Morpheus means, asking 'What does that mean?'
what_changes.after: Confronted with a reality he cannot reconcile, as Morpheus presses him on the difference between dreamworld and the real world.
what_changes.evidence: Have you ever had a dream, Neo, that you were so sure was real?

what_changes.before: Under control, monitored, with the crew working methodically to pinpoint his location.
what_changes.after: In medical crisis, the operation racing against his failing body.
what_changes.evidence: TRINITY: It's going into replication. ... TRINITY: He's going into arrest!

what_changes.before: Unable to complete the lock, reporting 'Still nothing.'
what_changes.after: Successfully targeting Neo's location just in time for the signal.
what_changes.evidence: APOC: Lock! I got him! APOC: Targeting... almost there.

event_hint.one_line: The crew races to trace and pull Neo out of the Matrix as his body goes into crisis, culminating in the signal that yanks him through.

objects_that_matter: headphones wired to an old hotel phone
uncertain: Whether Neo survives the arrest or what exactly lies in the darkness he is swallowed into.
Whether the mirror's liquefaction is a physical event in the room or a manifestation inside Neo's perception of the Matrix.
What 'Tank' and 'the signal' concretely are beyond Morpheus's call for them.

minds.wants: To hold onto something solid — a fixed point of 'real' — while everything he trusts about his senses dissolves.
minds.feels: A vertiginous terror that is also, underneath, a kind of surrender; he is being unmade and part of him recognizes this as the thing he came for. His panic ('Uh-oh...', 'It's cold') is the body's revolt, but his curiosity never fully leaves him — he keeps *watching*, even as he sinks.
minds.shows: Wide-eyed staring, whispered questions to Trinity ('You did all this?'), the small-boy 'Uh-oh', the physical struggle to keep his mouth above the crawling gel. He lets the awe show more than the fear until the arrest, when the body takes over entirely.
minds.basis: He whispers 'You did all this?' to Trinity with what reads as admiration, then fixates on the mirror healing and touches it despite the danger; his 'Did you...?' and 'This can't be...' are attempts to reconcile, and 'Uh-oh' is a near-wry acknowledgment rather than a scream until the cold and the arrest overwhelm him.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus is a guide who will explain the truth to him and keep him safe through it.
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus is conducting an extraction that Neo was never fully briefed on — the 'trace program' is really the mechanism of his unplugging, and Morpheus's calm pedagogy masks that Neo is being pushed into a medical crisis ('going into arrest') that Morpheus treats as a routine step.

believes_about.belief: That Trinity, the one who touched him gently and built all this, is a protector he can lean on.
believes_about.wrong_because: Trinity warned him in the hall to 'be honest' and is here as the crew's monitor, not his advocate; her tenderness is real but subordinate to the operation, and she will be the one reading his body fail without being able to stop it.

believes_about.belief: That 'this can't be real' — that his senses are still a reliable court of appeal against what he's seeing.
believes_about.wrong_because: This is exactly the question Morpheus is dismantling; the whole scene exists to prove that the feeling of 'real' is the last and most deceptive thing to let go of, so his instinct to reject it is the very illusion being dissolved.

minds.wants: To carry Neo across the threshold of disbelief and get him out — the philosophy and the extraction are one motion, and he will not let Neo's panic derail either.
minds.feels: A disciplined, almost ceremonial focus; he is doing the thing he has waited years for (the 'look' he read in Neo's eyes in the previous room is being acted on now), and there is steel under the calm — when the body fails he swears ('Shit!') but never loses command.
minds.shows: Socratic calm — he answers Neo's terror with questions ('Be real?', 'How would you know...?'), times his instructions to the crew around Neo's dissolution, and only breaks into urgency when the monitors scream. He lets Neo see a teacher, not an operator.
minds.basis: He continues the Alice/dream rhetoric from sc-029 seamlessly into the physical unmaking, never explaining the pill's true function in plain terms ('What does that mean?' goes unanswered by him, deflected to Cypher), and he keeps drilling the dreamworld/reality distinction even as Neo's fingers melt — the pedagogy is the point, not reassurance.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is ready — that the 'look in his eyes' means he can take this and come through it whole.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo is going in largely on faith and awe, not comprehension; his 'What does that mean?' and 'Uh-oh' show a man being dragged faster than he understands, so Morpheus's confidence in Neo's readiness is partly a projection of his own hope (see ev-010, where he admits he broke a rule freeing an older mind).

believes_about.belief: That Trinity will hold the line on Neo's body so he can hold the line on Neo's mind.
believes_about.wrong_because: Trinity is doing exactly that, but the scene shows her losing that race ('going into arrest'); Morpheus's trust is warranted in her skill yet the operation still nearly kills Neo before Apoc gets the lock.

minds.wants: To keep Neo alive through a procedure that is turning lethal faster than the targeting can finish — her job has just flipped from guide to monitor.
minds.feels: Tightening alarm under a trained exterior; she is the one who can see the numbers going wrong, and there is the strain of someone who vouched for this man (she brought him, she touched him, she told him to be honest) now watching his vitals collapse.
minds.shows: Professional brevity — she nods to his 'You did all this?', seats the headphones, and then speaks only in clinical readings ('It's going into replication', 'I got fibrillation', 'He's going into arrest'). She does not comfort him; she reports him.
minds.basis: Her dialogue narrows from a single human nod to pure medical triage as the crisis mounts; she is the axis on which 'safety → medical crisis' turns, and her restraint — never once addressing Neo by name or reassuring him as his body fails — is the visible discipline of someone doing her job under pressure.

believes_about.belief: That this candidate might actually be the one — enough that she broke protocol to bring him and now fights to keep him.
believes_about.wrong_because: Unknown to her in the moment: the procedure she's running to save his body is only the beginning of what Morpheus believes Neo is; her investment in him personally is ahead of any proof he is 'the One.'

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus knows exactly what he's doing and the risk is contained.
believes_about.wrong_because: The arrest suggests the risk is not fully contained; her escalating readings are the evidence that even Morpheus is improvising against a body that is failing faster than the crew can target.

minds.wants: To get the lock before Neo dies on the table — he is the bottleneck between a man arresting and a man being pulled free.
minds.feels: Mounting pressure and a hit of relief when the lock lands; he carries the specific dread of being the one whose delay could cost Neo his life.
minds.shows: terse status reports — 'Almost', 'Still nothing', 'Targeting... almost there', then the release of 'Lock! I got him!' — his emotional arc is entirely compressed into the success or failure of a signal.
minds.basis: His standing shifts from failure ('Still nothing') under Morpheus's repeated 'Apoc?' to success ('Lock! I got him!') exactly when Morpheus can call 'Now, Tank, now!', and the whole crew's timing hinges on his lock, so his interior state is legible purely through the targeting updates.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is a package to be located and extracted — a target to lock, not a person he's watching dissolve.
believes_about.wrong_because: Reducing Neo to a signal is exactly what lets Apoc do his job under the horror of it; but Neo is a man going into cardiac arrest inches away, and the dehumanizing frame is a coping mechanism, not the whole truth.

minds.wants: To deflect Neo's fear (and his own) with a joke, and to stay busy enough not to dwell on what this extraction really costs.
minds.feels: A weary, sardonic distance — he has done this before and knows where it ends; the flippancy ('buckle up, Dorothy') is the armor of someone who stopped being awed long ago.
minds.shows: A single crack at Neo, then he returns to 'checking reams of phosphorescent data' with Apoc; he offers no explanation, no comfort, no awe. He lets Neo see a smartass, which is easier than letting him see a tired man.
minds.basis: He is the only one who answers Neo's 'What does that mean?' and does it with a Wizard of Oz quip instead of an explanation, then disappears back into the data — the deflection is character-revealing, especially against the others' intensity, and foreshadows a man whose relationship to this work is already corroded.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is just another 'Dorothy' — a fresh mark about to be yanked out, nothing special, all wide eyes.
believes_about.wrong_because: This is the seed of Cypher's later betrayal (his resentment of the whole enterprise grows from exactly this kind of dismissiveness); he writes Neo off as routine, which blinds him to why Morpheus and Trinity are investing so much.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus's faith is another round of the same ritual, a leader playing prophet for another ordinary rescue.
believes_about.wrong_because: Cypher's cynicism can't see that this time may be different; his flattening of Morpheus into 'just doing Morpheus things' is the fault line that will later open into his deal to be reinserted.

minds.wants: To keep her station in the crew and get Neo out — same as everyone, but from a place of no-nonsense competence rather than investment.
minds.feels: Watchful readiness; she is present and working but the scene gives her no line, so her interior is a held posture rather than an arc — alert, contained, letting the others carry the drama.
minds.shows: Nothing legible beyond presence; she looks up when they enter and works. There is no concealment here, only absence of focus.
minds.basis: She is named present and 'looking up as they enter' and is part of the crew hardwiring the system, but the scene assigns her no dialogue and no reaction beat; to invent an arc for her would be to fill the field, so this reading is deliberately thin and flagged.

connects_back: Morpheus's 'look of a man who accepts what he sees because he is expecting to wake up' (sc-029) is being acted upon here — the mirror-liquid is the literalization of 'you can't wake from this dream,' and Morpheus's dreamworld/reality interrogation is the direct continuation of his sc-029 catechism.

Trinity's hallway warning 'Be honest. He knows more than you can possibly imagine' (sc-028) pays off in Neo's bewildered honesty ('What does that mean?', 'Uh-oh') and in the crew's refusal to soften what he's undergoing.
The red pill Neo took before entering (sc-029's cliffhanger) is now explained as the 'trace program' that disrupts his carrier signal — the physiological unmaking is the consequence of that choice.

Neo's awe at Morpheus ('You're a legend', sc-029) surfaces as the whispered 'You did all this?' to Trinity — he is still processing these people as mythic, which is why the horror lands so late for him.
sets_up: Neo's body failing (arrest, fibrillation) makes necessary his emergence naked, bald, and helpless in the pod (ev-006) and his atrophied-muscle reconstruction on the Nebuchadnezzar (ev-008) — the unplugging is physically brutalizing, not clean.

The 'Tank / the signal' that yanks Neo into darkness sets up his transport through the waste system and awakening on the hovercraft (ev-007), where he will first meet the real crew and his own ruined body.

Morpheus's willingness to push a barely-prepared Neo into a near-fatal extraction sets up his later apology for breaking the rule against freeing older minds (ev-010) — the risk he took here is the risk he will have to answer for.
Cypher's dismissive 'Dorothy' framing of Neo, and his corroded flippancy about the work, plant the resentment that will later drive his betrayal (ev-010's world).
dramatic_function: This is the threshold scene that converts Morpheus's abstract philosophy into visceral, bodily fact: it dramatizes 'waking from a dream you can't wake from' by making Neo's own senses and body betray him, so the audience experiences the collapse of 'real' rather than being told about it. It also shifts the story from seduction (sc-029) to consequence — every character's relationship to the operation (Morpheus's faith, Trinity's investment, Cypher's cynicism, Apoc's pressure) is established in miniature, and Neo's near-death raises the real cost of the freedom he asked for.
